01 — The Challenge

The raw export was unusable for reporting

The source sheet mixed casing conventions ("consumable" vs "Consumables"), left order status and region blank on ~18 rows, stored unit counts as text ("~218", "236 pcs"), repeated 6 Sale IDs, and carried typos across product names. None of it could feed a pivot table reliably as-is.

Medical Sales Data — raw source table, 200 rows × 15 columns
02 — The Process

A repeatable cleaning pass, field by field

Every column got a rule, not a one-off fix, so the same logic holds if new rows are appended later.

  1. Standardized categorical textCategory, Region, Order Status and Payment Method were trimmed, case-normalized, and mapped to a single canonical spelling (e.g. "consumable" / "Consumables" → one value).
  2. Filled every blankMissing Region, Payment Method and Order Status were set to an explicit "Unspecified" rather than left null, so nothing silently drops out of a pivot or slicer.
  3. Fixed duplicate Sale IDs6 IDs were reused across two different orders (e.g. MED‑0011 appeared twice). Each duplicate was reassigned to the matching gap in the ID sequence.
  4. Converted Units Sold to numericValues like "~218" and "236 pcs" were stripped of stray characters and cast to whole numbers so SUM/AVERAGE formulas work correctly.
  5. Corrected product-name typosEntries like "Adult iaper", "AED Bttery" and "Saline Bg 500ml" were matched against the product catalog and corrected, with acronyms (IV, ECG, CPAP, AED) kept uppercase.

03 — The Dashboard

An interactive view for sales performance

Built on a PivotTable layer with two category/region slicers, a 36‑month sales trend, and status, sector, region and rep breakdowns — all driven by the cleaned data so every chart stays accurate.

Sales Dashboard — slicers, monthly trend, and breakdowns by sector, region and representative

05 — Data Model

A helper layer that keeps the dashboard honest

Rather than pointing PivotTables straight at the raw export, a dedicated Dashboard Data sheet holds the cleaned, typed columns the dashboard actually reads from — separating "what came in" from "what gets reported on."
